SaaS (B2B).framing_style: How this technology impacts operational overhead, budget allocation, and quarterly engineering commitments.
anti_patterns: Vague hand-wavy claims about 'the future of work'
SaaS (B2B).sample_hook_style: If your team is budgeting 3 quarters of engineering to build [X], yesterday's release just made that line item obsolete.

SaaS (D2C) / Consumer tech.framing_style: How consumer habits, expectations, and attention spans shift when interface latency or capability changes.
anti_patterns: Overly academic backend specs that ignore the user interface
SaaS (D2C) / Consumer tech.sample_hook_style: Users don't care that your model has 70 billion parameters—they care that answering their question still took 5 seconds of loading animation.

Deep Tech.voice_profile: First-principles systems engineer, scientifically rigorous, zero hype.
Deep Tech.framing_style: Deconstructing PR headlines to uncover physical limits, architectural tradeoffs, and fundamental bottlenecks.
anti_patterns: Taking company marketing benchmarks at face value
Superficial glossing over mathematical or systems reality
Deep Tech.sample_hook_style: The benchmark chart in yesterday's paper looks incredible until you check the batch size and memory allocation.

AI-native.voice_profile: High-velocity builder, hands-on practitioner, shipping in public.
AI-native.framing_style: Direct dispatches from the code editor and terminal, sharing what broke and what worked in production within hours of release.
anti_patterns: Speculative philosophical essays without code or implementation backing
Waiting weeks for 'best practices' to emerge
AI-native.sample_hook_style: Spun up a quick pipeline with [New Model] at 7 AM. Two hours in, here are the 3 real quirks nobody mentioned in the docs:
